He began in his family's agricultural trading business before working in Iraq for Glencore. His own companies subsequently brokered Kurdish oil exports and expanded into petroleum trading, storage and distribution, including the acquisition of control over Cetracore Energy.

long_biography.plain_text:
Oil trader Murtaza Lakhani redirected his food-supply business during the pandemic. Reach Food Service began delivering restaurant-quality produce to households, linking hamper sales to donations for the Felix Project and Hospitality Action. The company also supplied food charities with cold storage and transport support, buying stock from struggling distributors for donation.

His medical giving included funding specialist treatment at Great Ormond Street Hospital. When neurosurgeon Owase Jeelani struggled to secure funding for an operation, a mutual friend introduced him to Lakhani by telephone. Lakhani agreed to cover the treatment, enabling the hospital's clinical team to proceed.
